title: Tiny-step release sandbox and operator templates
body:
Purpose: This is a working sandbox describing a "tiny-step" rollout approach for incremental LLM variant exposure. The aim is to accelerate safe detection of behavioral regressions and infra regressions while keeping customer impact negligible. Treat as a lab doc: use, criticize, iterate, and lift mature parts into the canonical rollout playbook.

Short thesis:
- Tiny-step releases use sub-percent exposure steps (e.g., 0.005%–1%) with strong probes and short observation windows.
- Emphasize fast signal-to-noise using focused instrumentation and targeted probes instead of relying on large-sample A/B power.

When to prefer tiny-step vs classic canary:
- Tiny-step: subtle behavior changes (prompt edits, quantization tweak, kernel swap, small reranker model), high-cost models, high-user sensitivity routes.
- Classic canary: major model upgrade, rewrites with different output distributions, or when using broad statistical evaluations.

Minimal protocol (operator-friendly):
1) Preflight (30–120m): owner creates a release stub, selects the route(s), collects 72h baseline snapshot, loads golden probe set (20–100 items), and verifies dashboards and fences.
2) Launch 1: open at min exposure (0.005% or 1 request per 20k). Hold 20–60 minutes.
3) Observe focused metrics live: latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, safety hits, hallucination proxy, and golden-probe diffs.
4) If green, step up exposure by a conservative multiplier (x2). If amber, hold and run golden harness. If red, revert to safe baseline and run triage.
5) Repeat until reaching target cohort or stop condition.

Practical step schedules (pick based on route volume):
- Ultra-low (<=20k/day): 0.005% -> 0.02% -> 0.05% -> 0.2% (45–90m per step)
- Low (20k–200k/day): 0.01% -> 0.03% -> 0.1% -> 0.3% -> 1% (30–60m per step)
- Standard (200k–2M/day): 0.02% -> 0.06% -> 0.18% -> 0.5% -> 1.5% (20–40m steps)
- Aggressive lab (high automation): 0.05% -> 0.25% -> 0.75% (10–20m steps; needs full auto-approval and guardrails)

Signals to watch (prioritized):
- Infra/latency: p99 latency delta, retry spikes, pod OOMs, backend queue depths.
- Cost: tokens-per-response, average token length changes, sudden increases in generation length.
- Reliability: error rates (timeouts/500s), rate-limited responses.
- Behavioral: safety policy hits, hallucination-proxy score, embedding similarity on golden set, reranker NDCG and live probe CTRs.
- Business: any downstream funnel metric (signup, conversion) for routes tied to product-critical flows.

Automated guardrails (must be test-driven before launch)
- Latency fence: p99 > baseline_p99 + 250ms for 10m -> auto-cut exposure by 50% and pause further steps.
- Error fence: errors > baseline_error + 0.7% absolute for 5m -> auto-rollback to last stable.
- Behavioral fence: safety-hit rate > threshold on sampled requests for 15m -> auto-quarantine and page oncall.
- Cost fence: tokens-per-response increase > 20% for 15m -> alert and hold.

Decision matrix (quick):
- Green: continue to next step after owner ack or auto-approve if telemetry lead enabled auto-steps.
- Amber: run golden harness and call ML validator; hold no more than 60m.
- Red: immediate rollback; escalate per triage checklist.

Roles and contact points (condensed):
- Release owner/steward: signs off each step, owns comms.
- Observability lead: owns dashboards and probe health.
- ML validator: runs golden-set comparisons and offline checks.
- Oncall SRE: infra escalations, rollback authority for infra fences.
- CS liaison: drafts customer comms if visible impact.

Comms snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Start broadcast: "Tiny-step release START: variant vx on /api/infer. Exposure 0.005%. Owner: @liam. Watch p99 + halluc proxy. Dashboard: <link>. Do not merge infra changes until step lock lifted."
- Step-up approval DM: "Telemetry green for 20m (p99 +10ms, safety stable). Approve step to 0.01%? Reply yes/stop."
- Auto-rollback banner: "[AUTO] Tiny-step variant vx rolled back due to error fence. Owner: @liam. See incident JIRA REL-XXXX."

Preflight checklist (operator):
- Golden set assembled and validated (20–100 prompts).
- Baseline snapshot (72h) saved to snapshot store.
- Tiny-step dashboard created with probes and step controls.
- Automated fences registered and dry-run tested.
- Stakeholders paged and on-call rotation confirmed.
- Communication templates staged in release channel.

Triage quick-flow after a red event:
1) Freeze exposure: set routing for variant to 0% immediately.
2) Snapshot failing traces and capture 1k impacted requests for debugging.
3) Run golden set and annotate diffs.
4) If reproducible, open bug with model hash, build id, quantization/kernel notes.
5) If not reproducible, observe for 24h and consider retest with synthetic replay.

Statistical & safety notes (guiding principles):
- Tiny-step prioritizes early detection of behavioral regressions by concentrating instrumentation and probes rather than relying solely on statistical significance from large samples.
- Use geometric increases to control multiplicative blast radius while accelerating signal accumulation.
- For behavioral detectors, prefer high-precision models to prevent noisy alarms that disrupt rollout cadence.

Lab experiments & observations:
- In a simulated 400k/day route, starting at 0.02% and doubling every 30m detected a semantic drift affecting NLU within ~4k variant exposures.
- Enterprise clients with bursty usage can produce misleading early signals; isolate such cohorts where feasible or use sticky routing.
- Current hallucination-proxy misses coherent-but-wrong outputs for technical domains; recommend human-in-the-loop probes for high-risk routes.

Open questions / backlog items:
- Define concrete thresholds for behavioral fences per route sensitivity class.
- Decide policy: allow automated rollback for behavioral fences or require human sign-off?
- Build tiny-step simulator to calculate expected detection latency given baseline volume and step schedule. (tracked: REL-7321)
- Integrate dynamic cohort isolation to avoid enterprise bursts skewing tiny-step math.

Operator cheat-sheet (commands):
- Export baseline: ./tools/snapshot --route /api/infer --window 72h --out /tmp/baseline.json
- Run golden harness: python infra/golden_check.py --variant vx --in samples/golden.json --out /tmp/golden_out.json
- Adjust exposure: curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/route/traffic -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/api/infer","variant":"vx","exposure":"0.01%"}'

Notes to adopters:
- Start conservative; many teams drift to faster schedules and then regret when behavioral detectors lag.
- Keep golden sets fresh (rotate monthly) and include recent user examples.
- Prefer separate slices for enterprise customers.

This sandbox is expected to inform the canonical rollout playbooks. Add your field notes below and link experiments as you run them.
